newsitem.title: CANADA: Bell Canada launches interactive telephone.
newsitem.headline: Bell Canada launches interactive telephone.

text.p: Bell Canada, the telephone company serving the Canadian provinces of Ontario and Quebec, launched a screen-based phone on Tuesday providing access to banking, movie reviews, sports scores and David Letterman's top 10.
The interactive telephone, developed by a joint venture owned by Northern Telecom Ltd. and Bruncor Inc. will cost C$295 ($221) to buy or C$9.75 ($7.32) for monthly rental.
Bell Canada marketing manager Tony Mandarino said the Vista 350 telephone with Direct Access services will be an alternative to the Internet for customers without home computers.
Most people who bought or rented the telephone in the marketing trials in London, Ontario, and Sherbrooke, Quebec, cited banking as its most attractive feature, Mandarino said.

Trials for an addition to the telephone that would allow access to cash through transfers to a computerized "smart card" are under way in the Ontario city of Guelph and will likely continue until the end of next year.

For now, customers can pay bills, transfer money between accounts or find mutual fund prices. They can also look at current movie listings and order tickets if the film is playing at a Cineplex Odeon theatre.

Only six retailers -- including Hudson's Bay Co. unit Zellers -- and four financial institutions -- Canada Trust, Royal Bank of Canada, Desjardins and National Bank of Canada -- have signed up. But Mandarino said others will soon be on the roster.
